mercy_translation.text:
The things we say are not confined to words; they also possess the testimony of truth from experience itself.

Let whoever wishes come and observe the sign of virtue in the virgins of Christ and in young people who practice chastity, and the faith in immortality in the great company of martyrs.

Let anyone who wishes to test what was said before approach the apparitions of demons, the deception of oracles, and the wonders of magic. Let that person use the sign of the cross which they mock and merely name Christ, and he will see how through him demons flee, oracles cease, and every kind of magic and sorcery is rendered ineffective.

Who, then, and how great is this Christ, who by his name and presence has overshadowed and abolished all these things from every side, who alone is strong against them all, and who has filled the whole inhabited world with his teaching? Let the Greeks who laugh so much and do not blush tell us.

If he is merely a human being, how did one human being surpass the power of all the gods among them and expose them by his own power as nothing? If they say he is a magician, how is it possible that through a magician all magic is abolished rather than established? If he had defeated individual magicians or prevailed over only one, they might reasonably have thought that he surpassed the others by a stronger art.

But if his cross has won the victory over every form of magic and even over its very name, it should be clear that the Savior is not a magician—especially since demons invoked by other magicians flee from him as their Master.

Who, then, is he? Let the Greeks, whose only concern is mockery, tell us. Perhaps they will say that he too was a demon and that this is how he had power. But in saying this they themselves deserve mockery and can again be put to shame by the earlier demonstrations. For how can the One who drives out demons himself be a demon?

If he merely drove out some demons, they might think that by the ruler of demons he had power over lesser ones, as the Jews once said in order to insult him. But if every demonic frenzy is cast out and pursued by the naming of Christ, it is clear that they are mistaken here too and that our Lord and Savior Christ is not some demonic power, as they imagine.

Therefore, if the Savior is neither merely a human being, nor a magician, nor a demon, but by his divinity has abolished and overshadowed poetic mythology, demonic illusion, and Greek wisdom, it should be evident and confessed by all that he truly is the Son of God, being the Word, Wisdom, and Power of the Father. For this reason his works are not merely human but beyond human and are recognized as truly God's works, both from what is visible and from comparison with human achievements.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The chapter appeals to ascetic life, martyrdom, and anti-magical claims as apologetic evidence within Athanasius' historical setting.
Mercy should contextualize ancient claims about demons, magic, and oracles rather than present them as modern empirical demonstrations.
